We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring which has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH (anilide). Actually the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an aniline with NH2). So the amide is attached to an aniline (para? not specified). So we need 3 steps retrosynthesis.

Given hints: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide via coupling (forward: amide formation). So retrosynthesis: break amide to carboxylic acid + amine.

2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. Retrosynthesis: break the double bond to give aldehyde + malonic acid.

3) Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we can propose route:

Target (A) = final product.

Step 1 (retro): disconnect amide C(=O)N linking the unsaturated chain to aniline. So we get precursor B: the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl (i.e., Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1?) Wait need to think: The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retro: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor B is the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl-sulfonamide core: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the unsaturated acid is /C=C/COOH? The Doebner modification yields α,β-unsaturated acid: Ar-CH=CH-COOH. In our target, we have Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (the amide). So the acid precursor would be Ar-CH=CH-COOH (where Ar is the phenyl-sulfonamide ring). So B: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1.

Step 2 (retro): The α,β-unsaturated acid can be derived from aromatic aldehyde (Ar-CHO) via Doebner with malonic acid. So break the double bond to give aldehyde (Ar-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor C: the aldehyde Ar-CHO (where Ar is same phenyl-sulfonamide). So C: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1.

Step 3 (retro): The sulfonamide group NS(=O)(=O) attached to the phenyl ring can be formed from amine (the phenyl with NH2) and sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride?). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the p-tolyl ring (the first phenyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl-sulfonyl group (p-tolyl-sulfonyl). The nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). Wait the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: p-tolyl (first ring) has substituent NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (as an aniline) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the p-tolyl aniline (i.e., p-toluidine). So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2...). The sulfonyl chloride would be ClSO2-Ph-... Wait typical sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. Here the amine is p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride is the aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated side chain (i.e., 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride). So retro: break sulfonamide to p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-... side chain). So precursor D: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). But we need a single molecule representation? In retrosynthesis tree, each reaction node can have multiple children (precursors). So step 3 will have two precursors.

Thus overall route: Target -> (amide formation) -> unsaturated acid + aniline; then (Doebner) -> aldehyde + malonic acid; then (sulfonamide formation) -> p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (which itself derived from aldehyde? Actually the aryl sulfonyl chloride is same as aldehyde after oxidation? Wait we already have aldehyde as precursor C. The sulfonyl chloride is derived from same aromatic ring but with sulfonyl chloride substituent instead of aldehyde? Actually the aldehyde is on the second phenyl ring (c2...). The sulfonyl chloride is also on that ring (ClSO2-). So they are different functionalizations of same ring. In retrosynthesis, we could have the sulfonyl chloride derived from the same aromatic ring via chlorosulfonation of the aldehyde? But we only have 3 steps total, so we need to incorporate sulfonyl chloride formation as part of step 3, not further disconnection. So step 3 will produce both p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (which is a commercially available reagent maybe). So we can stop there.

Thus we need to find template IDs for each reaction type.

We need to search for templates matching amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Use functional groups broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid; formed: amide. But earlier search returned none. Maybe need to use "amide" as formed and "aliphatic carboxylic acid" broken. That gave empty. Could be because the product is amide, but the template expects specific pattern. Could try search with "carboxylic acid" broken and "amide" formed? But "carboxylic acid" not valid; need "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Already used. Maybe need to search for "primary amines" broken? Actually amide formation breaks carboxylic acid O-H and forms C-N. The broken functional group is "aliphatic carboxylic acid". That is correct. Yet no templates. Could be that the database doesn't have that specific transformation. Could try search for "amide" formed only, maybe get templates that include amide formation. Already did, got none. Could try "primary amines" broken? Not broken. Let's search for "acyl chloride" formed? Not.

Maybe we can use generic amide coupling template ID from known dataset. Could try to search for reaction where product contains "C(=O)N" and reactants include "C(=O)O" and "N". Let's search for template with product containing amide. Use search without functional groups? Provide molecule_smiles of target amide? Let's try search for template where product is "C(=O)N" pattern. Use molecule_smiles "C(=O)N". Already did. No results. Could be that the database requires specifying functional groups broken/formed. Maybe we need to specify "carboxylic esters" broken? Not.

Alternative: Use "apply_template" later to verify. But we need template IDs for route. Could we use generic known template IDs from literature? Not.

Maybe we can use Doebner modification template. Search for functional groups: broken: "aldehydes"? formed: "C-C double bonds". Let's try.
